# BCNU 2025–2029 Settlement — What You GAIN / What You GIVE UP

**A plain-language guide for your ratification vote.** Every line below is sourced to the
settlement booklet (PDF page) and the clause it changes. This is built to be *honest first,
persuasive second* — the wins are real, but so are the give-ups and the fine print, and you
should see all of it before you vote.

*Independent and unofficial — not affiliated with BCNU/NBA, and not advice. **AI-assisted
(Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.8) and human-directed**, then cross-checked against the official
documents (full method in
[METHODOLOGY.md](METHODOLOGY.md)). The whole project is public and version-tracked on GitHub —
every change is logged with a date and a reason, so nothing is edited quietly. Where this guide
and the official documents disagree, the official documents govern — verify anything that
matters before you vote.*

> **How to read this:** ✅ = a gain · ❌ = a loss / give-up · ➖ = housekeeping (no change to
> what you get) · ⚠️ = a catch worth knowing (a condition, a cap, or a gain that doesn't start
> until 2026/2027/2028). Term of the deal: **April 1, 2025 → March 31, 2029** (4 years).
> Most provisions take force **30 days after ratification** unless a later date is noted.

---

## At a glance

| | Count | What it means |
|---|---:|---|
| ✅ **Gains** | **112** | New/larger pay, premiums, leave, benefits, protections. *(Note: ~16 of these are individual health-benefit line-item upgrades in one MOA — real, but small each.)* |
| ❌ **Losses / give-ups** | **9** | Removed or reduced entitlements, or new employer rights at your expense. |
| ➖ **Neutral / admin** | **63** | Renumbering, gender-neutral wording, restatements, committees, verbatim relocations. |
| ⚠️ **Watch-outs** | **69** | Conditions, caps, time-limited pilots, and **deferred** gains that phase in 2026–2028. |

**The honest summary:** this is a gains-heavy deal led by guaranteed wage increases, richer
premiums, expanded leaves, and a major reshaping of the benefits plan. But a real chunk of the
headline money **doesn't arrive until 2027–2028**, the benefit plan moves to a **formula-funded
trust** instead of a fixed employer guarantee, the new **Shift-Select Positions** trade scheduling
protections for flexibility, and a handful of older MOAs and protections were **deleted or quietly
thinned**. Details below.

---

## 🏆 Top wins

1. **Guaranteed wage increases: 3% + 3% + 3% + 3%** — effective the first pay period after
   **Apr 1 2025, 2026, 2027, 2028** (~**12.5% compounded** over the term). 2025/2026 are
   retroactive on ratification; **2027 and 2028 are still in the future.**
   *(Art 63 A.1, PDF p.116)*
2. **$100M / $200M / $300M in new provincial staffing funding** for minimum nurse-to-patient
   ratios across **FY2026/27, FY2027/28, FY2028/29** (and ongoing). *(mNPR Funding MOA, cl.1 —*
   ⚠️ *DRAFT, paid to health authorities, not guaranteed dollar-for-dollar to nurses.)*
3. **Regular premium up ~67%: $2.15 → $3.00 (2026) → $3.20 (2027) → $3.60 (2028)**; evening
   premium rises too; **missed/recalled meal penalties double from 1.5× to 2×.**
   *(Art 28.05 / 26.03, PDF p.69–73 — all phase in 2026+.)*
4. **Health-benefit upgrades**: LTD earnings threshold **$5,843 → $8,318 (RN/RPN) / $5,110
   (LPN)**, threshold now re-indexed every 2 years, plus a slate of plan improvements; backed by
   a **$175M NBA seed contribution** into a new union-influenced benefits trust.
   *(H&W Benefits MOA, PDF p.179–187 — effective Apr 1 2027, contingent on a Trust Agreement.)*
5. **New and bigger leaves**: Indigenous Child Care Leave **up to 62 weeks** (Apr 2026); new
   **Reservists' Leave**; paid compassionate leave **5 → 6 days**; a citizenship-ceremony day
   (Apr 2027). *(Arts 47, 37, 33, 43)*
6. **Casual Hours Incentive: up to $2,430/yr** for high-hours casuals ($1,000 at ≥600 hrs).
   *(Art 11.04(L), PDF p.54 — starts Jan 1 2027.)*
7. **Stronger safety law**: new enforceable duties on exposure to drugs/biohazards, plus new
   **sexual & domestic violence** and **violence-risk-mitigation** protections.
   *(Art 32.03(D)/32.07/32.08, PDF p.79–84)*
8. **Anti-agency-nurse protections** (your shifts offered first; agency nurses can't supervise
   you), **accommodation-first duty** on the Employer, and **layoff protection extended to AI /
   tech changes.** *(Art 6.02, App A.6, Art 20.01)*
9. **Overtime by seniority** for all pre-booked OT >48h out (precondition removed); **+1
   full-time steward** (Comox & Campbell River); **EDMP disability reps 22 → 24.**
   *(Art 27.07, App W, App A.2)*

## ⚠️ What you give up (and the big catches)

1. **Hidden reduction — Red-Circled wage protection.** When Appendix EE was folded into the
   articles, the **Classification Transition / Red-Circled** rule was cut down to a vague
   2-sentence paraphrase in Article 62 — dropping the "Green-Circled" status, the **March 31 2019**
   protection date, the paid-at-higher-level mechanics, the forfeiture conditions, and "increment
   progression continues." Presented as "housekeeping." *(App EE §3.b → Art 62, PDF p.145/148)*
2. **Deleted MOAs.** Six appendices struck — most are spent, but **Appendix Q** (path for
   home-support nurses to convert to **regular status**) and **Appendix JJ.2** (a **specialty-
   education funding floor**) carried live value with no shown replacement. *(General Housekeeping
   MOA, PDF p.155–209)*
3. **Shift-Select Positions trade protections for flexibility.** SSP nurses pick shifts by
   seniority, but **most of Article 25's scheduling protections are switched off**, SSP shifts
   earn **no overtime**, peak-period hours can be **mandatory**, and the new position type **risks
   eroding fixed lines.** *(Art 17, PDF p.59–60)*
4. **Benefits become a formula-funded trust.** Article 60's fixed, 100%-employer-paid guarantees
   are replaced by an **Employer-Funded Nurses' Benefits Trust** funded by a %-of-payroll formula;
   **trustees can amend the plan**, and **massage is newly capped at $4,000.** Union gets more
   control; the employer's open-ended cost guarantee goes away. *(H&W MOA + EFNBT formula, p.179–197)*
5. **mNPR: a legal give-up.** In exchange for the staffing funding, the **NBA waives all disputes**
   over the Ministry's compliance with the 2023 ratios MOU up to now. *(mNPR MOA, cl.6)*
6. **Small cuts**: union bulletin-board print ratio cut (Art 6.08); **isolation travel allowance
   frozen at $150/mo** for the whole 4-year term (Art 54).
7. **A lot of the money is deferred.** None of the premium-dollar increases hit at ratification;
   wage years 3–4 and most benefit upgrades land in **2027/2028** (see fine print).

---

## ⚠️ Watch-outs & fine print

**Two unmarked "silent edits" in the booklet** (the change wasn't underlined, so a reader
trusting the markup would miss it — both confirmed against the in-force contract):
- **Art 16.03(A):** the words **"by the Employer"** were added, unmarked, to who removes/destroys
  disciplinary records after 18 months. Likely benign, but slipped in untracked. *(PDF p.57)*
- **Appendix XX:** a capitalized **"The"** was inserted, unmarked, to restart a sentence. Cosmetic.
  *(PDF p.156)*

**Restatements that are NOT cuts (don't be misled either way):**
- **Indigenous ceremonial leave "5 days → 37.5 hours"** (Art 46.02) is the *same* entitlement —
  1 day = 7.5h, so 5 days = 37.5h. FTE-neutral. *(Compressed-week staff should confirm.)*
- Large strike-throughs in **Appendix EE** are mostly **verbatim relocations** into Arts 6/11/13/18
  — no loss there (the real loss is the Red-Circled reduction, give-up item #1 above).
- **COLA (Appendix VV) deletion is NOT a forward-looking loss.** The Cost-of-Living Adjustment
  only ever applied to April 2023 and April 2024 — it was already spent. Deleting it in 2025
  removes nothing you'd have received over 2025–2029. *(App VV, PDF p.154–155; confirmed obsolete.)*
- **Gender-affirming medical leave (8 weeks paid) is NOT new.** It was already in the in-force
  contract (effective **April 1, 2023**, Appendix AAA). The only thing this round changes in that
  appendix is a **180-day deadline for inclusive bathroom/changeroom signage** — so don't read the
  8-week leave as a 2025–2029 win. *(App AAA, PDF p.162–163.)*

**Gains that DON'T start at ratification (deferred):**
- Wage increases **Year 3 (Apr 1 2027)** and **Year 4 (Apr 1 2028)**.
- **All premium-dollar increases** (Art 28) — first ones Apr 1 2026.
- Meal-penalty 2× rate (Art 26.03) — Apr 1 2026.
- **Health-benefit upgrades + LTD changes** — Apr 1 2027, *contingent on a Trust Agreement by
  Jul 1 2026* (Vince Ready mediation if not reached).
- **Casual Hours Incentive** — Jan 1 2027.
- **Indigenous Child Care Leave** — Apr 1 2026. **Citizenship-ceremony day** — Apr 1 2027.
- **EDMP reps 22→24** and **new isolation-travel communities** — Apr 1 2027.
- **Professional Responsibility Clause** goes operative — by **Nov 30 2026** (wording still TBD).
- **Shift-Select Positions** — no stated effective date beyond ratification.

**Time-limited pilots (end ~2029, no rollout guaranteed):**
- **Weapons-screening pilot** — 4 sites only, mostly voluntary, $3.73M funded, report-only.
- **Regional Joint OHS Committees pilot** — 2 years, continuation self-assessed.
- **BCHOA Rapid Dispute Resolution** — trial to **Mar 30 2029**; decisions set no precedent and
  use a stripped-down process (10-min submissions, no witnesses).

**"Working groups / committees" with no direct entitlement** (study bodies, may not deliver in
the term): Indigenous Grievance & Arbitration WG, Indigenous Workforce Committee, DEI WG,
**BCCNM Certified Practice WG** (need not even form until Apr 1 2028).

# Article 63 – Wage Schedules — Gains & Losses
Source: `changes/article-63-wage-schedules.md` · Baseline: `current/sections/article-63-wage-schedules-a-1-general-wage-increases.md`

**Tally:** ✅ 3 gains · ❌ 0 losses · ➖ 1 neutral · ⚠️ 2 watch-outs

## ✅ Gains
- **3% / 3% / 3% / 3% General Wage Increase (≈12.5% compounded over 4 years)** — guaranteed across-the-board GWI on every level and step, effective the first pay period after **April 1 2025, April 1 2026, April 1 2027, April 1 2028**. This is a brand-new 4-year wage ladder replacing the expired 2022–2024 schedule. *(A.1, PDF p.116)*
- **New "Correctional Health Services" premium** — nurses working in Correctional Health Services get a **2%** premium (of the Level 3, Fourth-Year hourly rate), effective first pay period after **April 1 2026** (deferred). The A.2 premium heading is also expanded to "Forensic and Corrections." *(A.2, PDF p.115)*
- **Existing Forensic premiums carried forward** — Forensic Nurse A keeps 4% (Level 3, 8th-yr rate); Forensic Nurse B / FCLNs keep 2% (Level 3, 4th-yr rate). No reduction. *(A.2, PDF p.115)*

## ➖ Neutral / Admin
- The full wage-rate grids (Levels 1–6 plus Pine Free Clinic, all four years, PDF p.117–132) carry **no tracked-change marks** — they are the clean tables produced by applying the 3% GWIs above. Nothing to itemize; the entitlement is the GWI %s and dates, not individual cells.

## ⚠️ Watch-outs
- **GWIs are partly retroactive, partly deferred.** Dated 2025/2026/2027/2028 with the deal signed May 2026 — Year 1 (Apr 2025) and Year 2 (Apr 2026) are effectively retroactive on ratification, while **Year 3 (Apr 2027) and Year 4 (Apr 2028) are future/deferred**. Nurses don't see those last two raises until those dates arrive. *(A.1, PDF p.116)*
- **Old COLA top-up is gone from the wage formula.** The struck 2022–2024 language included "additional GWI of up to 1.25% / up to 1%" COLA riders; the new 3%/yr GWIs are fixed with **no COLA rider** attached. Note: those riders only ever applied to April 2023/2024 (already spent — see the appendix-vv summary), so this is **not a forward-looking loss** — it just means the 2025–2029 term has fixed raises and no CPI-triggered top-up. *(A.1 struck text, PDF p.116)*

# Article 62 – Wage Schedule Classifications — Gains & Losses
Source: `changes/article-62-wage-schedule-classifications.md` · Baseline: `current/sections/article-62-wage-schedule-classifications.md`

**Tally:** ✅ 0 gains · ❌ 1 loss · ➖ 1 neutral · ⚠️ 2 watch-outs

> Note: two of the items below (Red-Circled paraphrase, Eagle Ridge) physically appear in a sibling changes file, `changes/appendix-ee-lpn-integration.md` (PDF p.148), but they substantively amend **Article 62 / superior benefits** and the cross-check tracks them as "Appendix EE → Article 62," so they are folded in here.

## ❌ Losses
- **LPN→RN/RPN move becomes a "promotion" (loses Art 18.06 shield).** Effective first pay period after **April 1 2026** (deferred), an LPN moving to an RN/RPN position WILL be treated as a promotion and WILL trigger Article 18.06 requirements — reversing the current rule that such a move is "not a promotion" and does "not trigger 18.06." Adds a process hurdle that today's nurses don't face when up-classifying. *(Art 62 amendment, PDF p.113)*

## ➖ Neutral / Admin
- Classification table, job groups (CH/DC/ED/PS), Level definitions, LPN Orthopaedic Technologist / LGN footnotes, and the OR-rate grandparenting language are restated unchanged. Adds the unchanged "merging…shall not result in any other changes" proviso. No entitlement change. *(Art 62, PDF p.113–114)*

## ⚠️ Watch-outs
- **HIDDEN LOSS — Red-Circled wage protection reduced to a 2-sentence summary.** The detailed "Classification Transition" protection from deleted Appendix EE §3.b is relocated into Article 62 as just: *"Upon integration into the NBA, certain LPNs were entitled to wage protection and received monetary increases. Effective April 1 2019, those identified LPNs had their wage rate 'Red-Circled'."* The paraphrase **DROPS** every operative protection: the interim **"Green-Circled"** status, the **March 31 2019** protection-end date, the Level-1-classified-but-paid-at-Level-2 mechanics, the **transfer/resign/retire forfeiture** condition, the **"special premium"** alternative, and **"wage increment progression continues."** The settlement calls this "housekeeping…not intended to substantively alter rights," but protections that existed in enforceable detail are now a vague restatement — verify against source PDF p.145 (struck §3.b) vs p.148 (Art 62 insert) before relying on it. *(appendix-ee changes file → Art 62 insert, PDF p.148)*
- **Eagle Ridge superior-benefit carve-out relocated (verify it survives).** The Eagle Ridge Hospital LPN superior-benefits guarantee from Appendix EE §1.b is re-inserted into Article 6.06; the broader "all other FBA/CBA superior benefits extinguished" language moves with it. Per the cross-check this moved verbatim (benign), but because both halves are wholly struck/added there is no inline diff — confirm the Eagle Ridge protection is intact. *(appendix-ee changes file → Art 6.06, PDF p.148)*

# Article 28 – Premiums — Gains & Losses
Source: `changes/article-28-premiums.md` · Baseline: `current/sections/article-28-premiums.md`

**Tally:** ✅ 4 gains · ❌ 0 losses · ➖ 1 neutral · ⚠️ 1 watch-out

## ✅ Gains
- **28.01(A) Evening premium** — $1.40 → **$1.90** (1st pay period after Apr 1, 2026), then **$2.15** (Apr 1, 2027), then **$2.32** (Apr 1, 2028). +66% over the term; all increases deferred to/after 2026. *(28.01(A), PDF p.72)*
- **28.05 Regular premium** — $2.15 → **$3.00** (1st pp after Apr 1, 2026), then **$3.20** (Apr 1, 2027), then **$3.60** (Apr 1, 2028). +67% over the term; all deferred. *(28.05, PDF p.73)*
- **28.06 Specialty premium — eligibility expanded** — $2.00/hr now also covers **NICU/PICU** (added to ICU/CCU line). Same dollar value, broader coverage. *(28.06(iii), PDF p.74)*
- **28.06 Level 1 OR & ER ortho-tech eligibility** — Effective 1st pp following Apr 1, 2026, **Level 1 nurses permanently assigned to OR**, and **Level 1 nurses assigned to ER as orthopaedic technologists**, become eligible for the $2.00 premium. Deferred. *(28.06, PDF p.74)*

## ➖ Neutral / Admin
- **28.01(B) Night premium** — Unchanged at **$5.00/hr**; the strike-through only removes the superseded Apr 2022 ($4.25) line. No new money. (28.02 Weekend, 28.03, 28.04 also show no change vs baseline.) *(28.01(B), PDF p.72)*

## ⚠️ Watch-outs
- **28.06 "Level 3/4/5 nurses permanently assigned"** — Old text covered "regular employees... employed in [dept] with permanently assigned staff." New text reframes eligibility as **Level 3/4/5 nurses permanently assigned to** the department. This restructure could narrow who counts as eligible (e.g., excludes employees below Level 3 in those units, except the explicitly re-added Level 1 OR/ER cases). Dollar value unchanged at $2.00. ⚠️ verify against final language. *(28.06, PDF p.74)*

# Article 26 – Hours of Work, Meal Periods, Rest Periods — Gains & Losses
Source: `changes/article-26-hours-of-work-meal-periods-rest-periods.md` · Baseline: `current/sections/article-26-hours-of-work-meal-periods-rest-periods.md`

**Tally:** ✅ 3 gains · ❌ 0 losses · ➖ 1 neutral · ⚠️ 0 watch-outs

## ✅ Gains
- **26.03(B)(2) Missed meal period** — When a nurse on a designated-available 7.5h shift is denied the 30-min meal break, the penalty rate rises from **time-and-a-half (1.5×)** to **double time (2×)** for the meal period. Effective 1st pp after Apr 1, 2026 (deferred); the existing 1.5× penalty remains until then. *(26.03(B)(2), PDF p.69)*
- **26.03(C) Recall during meal (not designated-available)** — Same upgrade: penalty for ungranted make-up time goes from **1.5× to 2×**. Effective 1st pp after Apr 1, 2026 (deferred). *(26.03(C), PDF p.69)*
- **26.03(D) Meal-period overtime cap raised** — The maximum overtime rate for meal periods rises from **1.5× to 2×** (irrespective of Article 27 rates). Effective 1st pp after Apr 1, 2026 (deferred); this lifts the cap so the new 2× penalties above can actually be paid. *(26.03(D), PDF p.70)*

## ➖ Neutral / Admin
- **26.03(B) list renumber** — Hand-corrected printed numbering error in the (B) list (printed (1),(1),(2) → corrected to (1),(2),(3) with negotiator initials). Cross-reference "(1) above / (2) apply" preserved. Pure renumbering, no substance. *(26.03(B), PDF p.69)*

# Article 27 – Overtime — Gains & Losses
Source: `changes/article-27-overtime.md` · Baseline: `current/sections/article-27-overtime.md`

**Tally:** ✅ 1 gain · ❌ 0 losses · ➖ 0 neutral · ⚠️ 0 watch-outs

## ✅ Gains
- **27.07 Overtime By Seniority — entitlement expanded** — Old text only applied "where a Health Authority/PHC has implemented automated call-in technology." # MOA – Health and Welfare Benefits — Gains & Losses
Source: `changes/moa-health-and-welfare-benefits.md` · Baseline: `current/sections/article-60-…`, `appendix-u/u.1/u.2-…`, `appendix-a` (LTD plan)

This MOA is a NEW instrument added wholesale. It (a) creates the **Employer-Funded Nurses' Benefits Trust (EFNBT)** to take over all health/welfare benefits effective **April 1, 2027**, (b) lists immediate plan enhancements (item 6), and (c) carries **Schedule 1** rewriting the Appendix A LTD plan. (Schedule 2 / Article 60 covered in its own summary.)

**Tally:** ✅ 16 gains · ❌ 1 loss · ➖ 2 neutral · ⚠️ 5 watch-outs

## ✅ Gains
- **Group Life $50,000 → $250,000** — 5× increase, effective on EFNBT commencement Apr 1 2027. *(item 6a, PDF p.179)*
- **AD&D $50,000 → $250,000** — 5× increase, effective Apr 1 2027. *(item 6b, PDF p.179)*
- **$25 annual EHC deductible removed** — extended health deductible eliminated. *(item 6c, PDF p.179)*
- **Hearing aids $1,000 → $2,500 per ear / 5 yrs** — 2.5× increase. *(item 6d, PDF p.179)*
- **Vision $350 → $900 every 24 months** — and now explicitly covers eye exams. *(item 6e, PDF p.179)*
- **Massage: $4,000/member + $2,000/dependent annual limit** — replaces scheduled cuts to $1,427 (2027) / $1,145 (2028); a large improvement vs. those impending limits, but a cap where the plan previously set **no massage-specific dollar limit** (see loss). *(item 6f, PDF p.179)*
- **Acupuncture $100 → $500 per person/yr** — 5× increase. *(item 6g, PDF p.179)*
- **Chiropractic $200 → $500 per person/yr** — 2.5× increase. *(item 6h, PDF p.179)*
- **Naturopathy $200 → $500 per person/yr** — 2.5× increase [handwritten JS initial]. *(item 6i, PDF p.179)*
- **Podiatry/chiropody $300 → $500 per person/yr** — increase; "$300" handwritten-corrected to "$400" then to $500 limit; "chiropody" struck, "podiatry" retained [JS]. *(item 6j, PDF p.179)*
- **Speech therapy $100 → $1,000 per person/yr** — 10× increase. *(item 6k, PDF p.179)*
- **Mental health (psych/RSW/RCC) $900 → $1,800 per person/yr** — doubled. *(item 6l, PDF p.179)*
- **Major dental coinsurance 60% → 70%** — plan pays more of major dental. *(item 6m, PDF p.179)*
- **Orthodontia lifetime max $2,750 → $4,000** — increase. *(item 6n, PDF p.179)*
- **Shingrex (shingles) vaccine added** — new coverage. *(item 6o, PDF p.179)*
- **LTD threshold $5,843 → $8,318 (RN/RPN) / $5,110 (LPN); indexing every 2 yrs (was 4)** — 70%/50% earnings-replacement breakpoint raised sharply for RNs/RPNs as of Apr 1 2024; reviewed every two years instead of four. (LPN figure $5,110 is below the old $5,843 — see watch-out.) *(Sch 1 §5.7 + item 6p, PDF p.187/179)*

## ❌ Losses
- **Massage benefit newly capped** — massage now carries a hard annual cap ($4,000/member, $2,000/dependent) where the EHC plan previously set **no massage-specific dollar limit**; the increased-cost amendments are part-funded "from savings from a reimbursement limit on massage therapy benefits." Net better than the looming Ready-decision limits ($1,427/$1,145) but a cap where there was none before. *(item 6f + item 6 chapeau, PDF p.179)*

## ➖ Neutral / Admin
- **LTD plan language relocated to the Trust** — Schedule 1 strikes most operative LTD text from Appendix A (eligibility detail, exclusions, application, residual benefit, ERIB, successive disabilities, premiums, administration, advisory committee) because those entitlements now sit in the EFNBT Trust/Plan Document; collective-agreement-governed obligations (waiting period, sick-leave top-up, benefit continuation, appeals/CRC, rehab/RRC, GRTW, return-to-work) are preserved. Substance moves, not deleted. *(Sch 1 §§1–23, PDF pp.184-191)*
- **"medical doctor or Nurse Practitioner"** — care-during-disability requirement updated to recognize NPs (minor scope expansion / admin). *(item 6q, PDF p.179)*

## ⚠️ Watch-outs
- **Benefits move into a trust funded by a formula, not a fixed employer guarantee** — equivalent to current HBT plan as of May 20 2026 plus the item-6 upgrades, but going forward governed by the Trust Agreement and Funding Formula. GAIN: dedicated funded trust + union/joint control over design. WATCH-OUT: no longer an open-ended employer promise to fund whatever the plan costs. *(items 2,5,6,9, PDF p.179)*
- **Trustees can amend the plan** — the item-6 upgrades "take effect immediately" but Trustees "will have authority to amend the benefit plan." Today's listed enhancements are not permanently locked. *(item 7, PDF p.179)*
- **NBA controls non-LTD design; LTD is joint; everything frozen until Apr 1 2029** — NBA trustees get exclusive amendment power over EHC/dental/life/AD&D; LTD amendments are joint NBA+HEABC; but before Apr 1 2029 ANY plan or administration change needs both HEABC and NBA agreement. *(item 8, PDF p.179)*
- **LPN LTD threshold ($5,110) is below the old single threshold ($5,843)** — RNs/RPNs gain ($8,318) but the LPN breakpoint is set lower than the prior uniform $5,843; for LPNs the 70%-replacement band is narrower than before. Confirm intent before characterizing as pure gain. *(Sch 1 §5.7, PDF p.187)*
- **Appendices S, T, U, U.1, U.2 terminated; deal is contingent and time-gated** — entire MOA is contingent on a mutually agreeable Trust Agreement by Jul 1 2026 (Vince Ready mediation if not); Appendix U/U.1/U.2 (incl. Ready massage limits) and Appendices S & T are terminated on signing the Trust Agreement / Apr 1 2027. If the Trust Agreement fails, the consequential amendments don't take effect. *(items 2,3,11,12, PDF p.179)*

## Deferred (post-ratification, conditional)
- All item-6 enhancements + Schedule 1 LTD changes: **effective Apr 1 2027**, contingent on a Trust Agreement (target Jul 1 2026). *(items 2,6,12, PDF p.179)*
- NBA non-LTD exclusive amendment authority + admin-cost / 0.2%-payroll mechanics: **Apr 1 2029**. *(item 8; key-terms 1,5, PDF p.179)*

NEW one-page "key terms" summary of the EFNBT. Benefit-enhancement items duplicate item 6 of the main MOA (not re-tallied here); this file adds the **funding/cost-allocation** terms. PDF p.181 (doc p.179).

- **NBA exclusive amendment authority over EHC, dental, life, AD&D from Apr 1 2029** — union control over benefit design. *(key term 1, PDF p.181)*
- **Employers pay full actual cost of EHC/Dental/Life/AD&D for first 2 years** — employer covers actual cost through EFNBT contributions Apr 2027–Mar 2029. *(key term 4, PDF p.181)*
- **Employer absorbs LTD experience risk** — employer increases contributions when LTD costs exceed projections by up to 2%, with further top-ups above 4%. *(key term 6, PDF p.181)*

- **EFNBT funded by employer % -of-payroll contributions, not a cost guarantee** — "designed with actuarial analysis for long-term sustainability"; sustainability now depends on the formula and trust management rather than an open-ended employer promise. *(key terms 3,5,6, PDF p.181)*

# EFNBT Funding Formula — Gains & Losses
Source: `changes/moa-efnbt-funding-formula.md` · Baseline: none (new instrument)

NEW standalone agreement (no tracked changes; all plain text) setting the numeric formula by which Employers fund the EFNBT. Executed May 21 2026. PDF pp.195-197 (doc pp.193-195).

**Tally:** ✅ 3 gains · ❌ 0 losses · ➖ 2 neutral · ⚠️ 4 watch-outs

## ✅ Gains
- **$175M NBA seed contribution, locked until after Mar 31 2029** — one-time Apr 1 2027 contribution for long-term sustainability; Trustees cannot draw on it to fund benefits before then, protecting the cushion. *(¶15, PDF p.196)*
- **Employer contribution rises 14.00% → 14.25% of payroll from Apr 1 2031** — defined, escalating employer funding. *(¶¶18-19, PDF pp.196-197)*
- **Employers retain liability for pre-Apr-1-2027 claims** — disability income/benefits for members disabled before Apr 1 2027, and EHC/dental/life/AD&D claims incurred before that date, stay an employer obligation at March 30 2025 plan levels until closed. *(¶¶10-12, PDF pp.195-196)*

## ➖ Neutral / Admin
- **Defined contribution rates** — Apr 2027–Mar 2029: 3.90% of payroll + actual EHC/Dental/Life/AD&D utilization, reconciled to actual annually; Apr 2029–Mar 2031: 14.00%; thereafter 14.25%. *(¶¶17-19, PDF pp.196-197)*
- **Allocation of pre-/post-transition responsibility + optional HBT asset/liability transfer** — EFNBT covers claims incurred after Mar 31 2027; HEABC/NBA may negotiate a transfer of HBT assets/liabilities. *(¶¶13-14, PDF p.196)*

## ⚠️ Watch-outs
- **Funding is a fixed %-of-payroll formula, not a cost guarantee** — after the 2-year reconciled startup, employer obligation is a flat 14.00%/14.25% of payroll; if real benefit costs outrun that, the gap falls on the trust (member-funded), subject only to the LTD risk-share. GAIN: predictable, defined funding + union control. WATCH-OUT: benefit security now depends on the formula holding. *(¶¶17-20, PDF pp.196-197)*
- **LTD risk-sharing is capped** — employer tops up only above a 3.90%-of-payroll baseline: ≤2% over → small uplift; 2–4% over → fixed 0.078% of payroll; >4% over → 0.078% plus 50% of the excess × 3.55%. Employers do NOT cover 100% of LTD overruns; residual LTD cost risk sits with the trust. *(¶¶21-23, PDF pp.196-197)*
- **Admin expenses above 0.2% of payroll shift to additional employer contribution only from Apr 1 2029** — within-0.2% admin is trust-funded. *(¶20, PDF p.197)*
- **"Payroll" base excludes premiums/allowances/differentials** — contributions computed on straight-time hours of regular employees only, narrowing the funding base. *(¶9, PDF p.195)*

## Deferred (post-ratification)
- Funding begins **Apr 1 2027**; $175M NBA contribution **Apr 1 2027** (usable after **Mar 31 2029**); rate step-ups **Apr 1 2029** and **Apr 1 2031**. *(¶¶15-19)*

# Article 17.0X – Shift-Select Positions (SSP) — Gains & Losses
Source: `changes/article-17-shift-select-positions.md` · Baseline: `current/sections/article-17-vacancy-postings.md` (Art. 17 "Vacancy Postings"; SSP is an entirely new clause)

**Tally:** ✅ 4 gains · ❌ 1 losses · ➖ 1 neutral · ⚠️ 5 watch-outs

This is a wholly NEW position type ("adding the following"). An SSP is a **regular position** (fixed 0.4–1.0 FTE) that is NOT tied to a fixed master rotation; the nurse selects shifts each booking window to make up their FTE. Read both the gains and watch-outs together — it expands flexibility but also creates an employer-controlled, schedule-unstable line that can absorb baseline FTE and relief work.

## ✅ Gains
- **Nurse-chosen schedule** — SSP nurses select their own shifts each booking window rather than working a fixed rotation; intended to improve flexibility, work-life balance, and control. *(intro + D, PDF p.59–60)*
- **Seniority-ordered selection** — Shifts are assigned in **seniority order** among SSP nurses; a 3-week selection process with a reselection round if a nurse doesn't get a full allotment. *(G, PDF p.60)*
- **SSP nurses bid ahead of casuals** — During SSP shift selection, SSP nurses bid on available shifts **in priority to casual employees**. *(F, PDF p.60)*
- **Stat & holiday protections retained** — Stat holidays are inserted into the booking window (M); SSP shifts on stat holidays are paid at Art. 39.03 holiday rates (P); vacation selected via a notional master-rotation line under Art. 45.04 (N). *(M/N/P, PDF p.60)*

## ❌ Losses
- **Most of Article 25 (Scheduling) is switched off** — Except 25.08, 25.09(A) and 25.10, **Article 25 does NOT apply to SSPs**; SSP shifts are not subject to normal scheduling requirements. Standard rotation/scheduling protections that regular-line nurses enjoy are largely removed for SSP nurses. *(O, PDF p.60)*

## ➖ Neutral / Admin
- **Catch-all** — Except as modified by this Article, all other Collective Agreement terms apply to SSP nurses; reassignment treated "the same as relief" and no more often than other employees. *(K, Q, PDF p.60)*

## ⚠️ Watch-outs
- **Could erode regular fixed lines** — SSPs can staff **regular baseline FTE** and operate as an "enhanced float/relief pool"; employers may use vacancy/overtime/agency data to decide where to convert staffing to SSPs. Risk: fewer predictable fixed-rotation lines over time. *(intro, A, PDF p.59)*
- **Employer can assign shifts you didn't pick** — If a nurse doesn't select enough shifts to make FTE by the deadline, the **Employer may assign** shifts within the work area to fill the FTE. Schedule control is conditional. *(J, PDF p.60)*
- **Limited overtime** — SSP shifts scheduled under this Article **will not incur overtime**; OT only on hours beyond scheduled shifts. Fewer OT opportunities than regular scheduling. *(P, PDF p.60)*
- **Mandatory peak-period work** — SSP nurses MUST select ≥75 hours × FTE during peak vacation periods (Spring Break and/or Dec 15–Jan 5). Constrains time off at the most-wanted periods. *(E, PDF p.59–60)*
- **Schedule instability / supernumerary fill** — If too few shifts of the required type exist, the nurse must take whatever remains, possibly **supernumerary relief shifts**; required night/evening/weekend minimums set by the posting and changeable only by mutual agreement. *(B, I, PDF p.59–60)*

# Article 32 – Occupational Health and Safety Program — Gains & Losses
Source: `changes/article-32-occupational-health-and-safety-program.md` · Baseline: `current/sections/article-32-occupational-health-and-safety-program.md`

**Tally:** ✅ 9 gains · ❌ 0 losses · ➖ 3 neutral · ⚠️ 4 watch-outs

## ✅ Gains
- **32.03(D), new** — New enforceable entitlement: where employees may be exposed to biological agents, chemicals, or substances (explicitly including **illicit/street drugs and unknown-composition substances**), the Employer must complete a risk assessment and, in consultation with the JOHSC, implement controls — may include a site-specific exposure control plan, training, and PPE. *(32.03(D), PDF p.79)*
- **32.03(E), new** — Biological exposure control plans must be built on the **precautionary principle** as defined by WorkSafeBC and informed by public-health guidance/orders. *(32.03(E), PDF p.79)*
- **32.03(F), new** — Express protection: **no employee may be disciplined for a refusal to work** when excused under the Workers Compensation Act / OHS Regulation. *(32.03(F), PDF p.79)*
- **32.03(C)** — OHS supervisory training is expanded to **annual refresher training** for employees performing supervisor duties, and must now cover the WCA, OHS Regulation, and supervisor roles/responsibilities. *(32.03(C), PDF p.79)*
- **32.05, new sub-clause** — New entitlement after a work-related traumatic incident: Employer must consult the employee and **can release them for the rest of the shift without loss of pay** and **provide transportation to medical care or home** if they can't travel safely. *(32.05, PDF p.81)*
- **32.06** — Psychological factors language tightened to "thirteen (13) **psychological** factors"; Employer's CSA Standard implementation must now **track future amendments** to the Standard. *(32.06, PDF p.82)*
- **32.06, new** — Health Authorities/PHC must **make available information and education** on workplace factors affecting psychological health and safety (hazard reduction + factors that promote it). *(32.06, PDF p.83)*
- **32.07, new clause (Sexual and Domestic Violence)** — Brand-new protection: Employer must revise/develop a sexual & domestic violence policy (reporting process, individualized safety plans, confidentiality, no adverse action for good-faith reports); must run a risk assessment + employee-centred safety plan when aware of risk; trauma-informed supports. *(32.07(a)-(c), PDF p.84)* **Note: policy due within 180 days of ratification — deferred.**
- **32.08, new clause (Violence Risk Mitigation)** — Consolidates and **strengthens** the prior violence provisions (relocated from 32.03(B)-(D),(F)): adds duty to communicate risks/measures to employees, broader hazard info-sharing covering **weapon use and threatening statements** plus pre-admission/transfer/care-transition notification, and a mandatory **post-incident investigation with corrective actions communicated to affected employees**. *(32.08(A)-(F), PDF p.83-84)*

## ➖ Neutral / Admin
- **Relettering & wording cleanup** — 32.03 clauses relettered (old E→B, G→C, H→D, J→E, K→F) after old (B)(C)(D)(F) moved to new 32.08; "healthful"→"healthy", "behavioral"→"behavioural", "&"→"and", PHC abbreviation, "j"→"J" capitalization. No substantive change. *(32.01/32.03/32.06, PDF p.75-83)*
- **JOHSC minutes mechanism modernized** — Replaces the old "request SWITCH BC develop a universal minutes format within 60 days" with onboarding to the **OHS Resource Centre**; minutes flow through the Centre once onboarded, monthly Union-copy obligation only applies pre-onboarding. Net process change, roughly neutral. *(32.01, PDF p.77)*
- **32.01 JOHSC rules of procedure** — Adds restatement that each JOHSC must establish its own rules of procedure per the WCA/OHS Regulation (codifies existing legal requirement). *(32.01, PDF p.75)*

## ⚠️ Watch-outs
- **32.07 sexual/domestic violence policy is a future deliverable** — the protection is a policy the Employer must produce **within 180 days of ratification**; the article sets requirements but the actual safety plans depend on that policy being written and applied. *(32.07(a), PDF p.84)*
- **Many duties are "consult JOHSC / raise concern" routes, not hard entitlements** — e.g., 32.03(D) controls are decided "in consultation with the JOHSC," and an employee's recourse if unhappy is to "raise their concern" via supervisor/JOHSC/reporting process — process, not a guaranteed outcome. *(32.03(D), PDF p.79)*
- **JOHSC info-disclosure depends on OHS Resource Centre onboarding** — the every-6-months data dump to the Union (Excel/.csv) only runs "until" JOHSCs onboard to the Resource Centre; after onboarding the Union relies on Centre access. Verify the Union retains equivalent visibility post-onboarding. *(32.01, PDF p.76-77)*
- **32.08 violence training is relocated, not net-new** — old 32.03(F) violence-prevention training language is moved verbatim into 32.08(F); confirm nothing was dropped in the move (it appears intact). *(32.08(F), PDF p.83-84)*

- **New 2-year pilot** — Establishes one **Regional OHS Committee** per Health Authority/PHC consolidating OHS, Psychological Health & Safety, and Violence Prevention into a single coordinated body — a modest structural gain for consistency/coordination. Commences within **120 days of ratification**. *(MOA ¶2-3, PDF p.172)*

## ➖ Neutral / Admin
- **Advisory body only** — Committee gives "guidance and recommendations" on policies, training, risk assessments, WorkSafeBC orders, and corrective actions; it is **not established under the Workers Compensation Act** and creates no individual entitlement. *(MOA ¶4 & ¶8, PDF p.172)*
- **Sample letter appended** — Non-binding NBA/HEABC support letter expecting terms-of-reference within 2 months of first meeting and ≥1 OHS project annually; sets expectations, not obligations. *(sample letter, PDF p.174)*

## ⚠️ Watch-outs
- **Time-limited pilot (2 years)** — At the end the committee self-assesses and decides whether to continue; no guarantee it survives. *(MOA ¶9, PDF p.172)*
- **Absorbs the Appendix G regional VP sub-committee** — for the pilot's duration the Regional OHS Committee **replaces and assumes** the obligations of the regional Violence Prevention sub-committee under Appendix G (Addressing Workplace Violence). If the pilot lapses, confirm the VP sub-committee role reverts cleanly. *(MOA ¶6, PDF p.172)*
- **Explicitly NOT an escalation pathway** — the MOA states it "is not an escalation pathway for local JOHSC concerns," so local committee issues do not gain a new route up through this body. *(MOA ¶6, PDF p.172)*

# MOA – Weapons Screening Pilot Project — Gains & Losses
Source: `changes/moa-weapons-screening-pilot-project.md` · Baseline: none (new instrument)

**Tally:** ✅ 2 gains · ❌ 0 losses · ➖ 1 neutral · ⚠️ 3 watch-outs

## ✅ Gains
- **New weapons-screening pilot** — First-time pilot of AI-based weapons detection and voluntary weapons screening as a proactive step against weapons-related violence in healthcare — a real safety gain at the pilot sites. *(MOA ¶1-3, PDF p.173)*
- **Dedicated funding** — Up to **$3.73 million** allocated from the OHS Fund (via Appendix A.1(A)) plus an additional **$100,000** for evaluation — funded, not aspirational. *(MOA ¶6, PDF p.173-174)*

## ➖ Neutral / Admin
- **Joint working group** — 4 Employer + 4 Union reps plus 1 Ministry of Health rep oversee the pilot and set evaluation metrics (cost-benefit, objects identified/surrendered, weapons incidents, injury rates, staff-perceived safety). Governance, not an entitlement. *(MOA ¶5, PDF p.173)*

## ⚠️ Watch-outs
- **Time-limited pilot, ~21 months** — Phase 1 planning (6 months) → Phase 2 implementation (1 year) → Phase 3 evaluation (within 3 months). Ends in a report only; no commitment to permanent rollout. *(MOA Phases 1-3, PDF p.173)*
- **Only 4 sites; screening is "voluntary" at 3 of them** — AI detection only at **Surrey Memorial (FHA)**; voluntary screening at **Vancouver General ED, UHNBC ED (Prince George), Kelowna General ED**. Most nurses see no change, and "voluntary" screening may limit protective effect. *(MOA Phase 2, PDF p.173)*
- **Expansion is only "discuss whether there is interest"** — adding further sites is not committed, just a commitment to talk about it. *(MOA ¶7, PDF p.174)*

# ARTICLE 6 – Union Rights and Activities — Gains & Losses

- **6.02 Agency-nurse limits (new B–E)** — Parties declare a "common interest in ending the use of private agency nursing." Employer must **offer all shifts to bargaining-unit nurses first** before using agency nurses; HEABC must give the NBA a **quarterly utilization report**; agency nurses/contractors **may not supervise or direct** NBA members. Real new protections against agency-nurse displacement. *(Art. 6.02(B)-(E), PDF p.44 / doc p.42)*
- **6.09 Steward time at orientation (15 min)** — Union steward now gets **up to 15 minutes** to address new hires at both in-person AND virtual orientations, paid (no wage/benefit deduction). *(Art. 6.09, PDF p.45 / doc p.43)*

# ARTICLE 16 – Employee Evaluation — Gains & Losses
Source: `changes/article-16-employee-evaluation.md` · Baseline: `current/sections/article-16-employee-evaluation.md`

**Tally:** ✅ 3 gains · ❌ 0 losses · ➖ 0 neutral · ⚠️ 2 watch-outs

## ✅ Gains
- **16.03(A) Automatic record removal** — Disciplinary records are now removed/destroyed **automatically** after 18 months. The old precondition "**Upon request of the employee**" is struck, so nurses no longer have to ask for stale discipline to be purged. *(Art. 16.03(A), PDF p.57 / doc p.55)*
- **16.03(A) Suspensions purged** — New sentence: suspension records **shall be removed and destroyed** 18 months after the suspension expires (old text only said they'd "remain on file for 18 months" — silent on destruction). Clear destruction obligation added. *(Art. 16.03(A), PDF p.57 / doc p.55)*
- **16.03(B) Letters of expectation purged faster** — Removal is now **automatic** ("Upon request" struck) and the clock drops from **18 months → 12 months**. *(Art. 16.03(B), PDF p.57 / doc p.55)*

## ⚠️ Watch-outs
- **⚠️ SILENT EDIT — "by the Employer" inserted (unmarked).** In 16.03(A) the booklet quietly added the words **"by the Employer"** to the removal/destruction clause ("...shall be removed **by the Employer** from the employee's file and destroyed..."). Only "shall" is underlined as a tracked change; **"by the Employer" is plain/unmarked**, so it does not show as an insertion. The current agreement reads only "...shall be removed from the employee's file and destroyed..." User-confirmed this is a genuine unmarked change in the source booklet. Likely benign (assigns who must act, supporting automatic removal), but it was slipped in untracked — verify and surface to voters. *(In 16.03(B) the same words "by the Employer" were also added, but there they ARE underlined/tracked as an insertion — the unmarked, silent edit is only in 16.03(A).)* *(Art. 16.03(A)/(B), PDF p.57 / doc p.55)*
- **New "16.X Employer Investigations" MOA — read both ways.** *Pro-nurse reading (✅):* adds process protections — Employer must **notify the Union** when a nurse is put on administrative leave pending a possible-discipline investigation, state the nature of the issue, work "in a timely fashion," and **explain any delay beyond 21 days**; results flow through the existing 9.06 / 15.04 protections. *Employer-right reading (⚠️):* it also formally **acknowledges the Employer's power to place nurses on administrative leave and investigate**, and the 21-day timeline is soft — delays are excused for "contingencies beyond the Employer's control," and the Employer may withhold detail it believes "could compromise the investigation." On balance it codifies notice/timeliness duties that did not previously exist, but it is not a hard deadline. Judge in light of Appendix references. *(Art. 16.X(A)-(D), PDF p.58 / doc p.56)*

# Appendix FF.1 – BCHOA Rapid Dispute Resolution Process Trial — Gains & Losses
Source: `changes/appendix-ff-1-bchoa-rapid-dispute-resolution.md` · Baseline: none (new instrument)

**Tally:** ✅ 2 gains · ❌ 0 losses · ➖ 0 neutral · ⚠️ 3 watch-outs

## ✅ Gains
- **Hearings within ~1 month, decisions within 14 days** — new streamlined RDR track for non-complex Art. 9.02 grievances: Registrar endeavours to schedule within one (1) month of referral; arbitrator may rule orally on the day, otherwise written decision within 14 calendar days. Much faster than full arbitration. *(clauses E, G; PDF p.~?, see note below)*
- **Either party can opt out** — Union or HEABC may pull any rostered file deemed unsuitable for RDR at any time before hearing and send it back to normal case management/arbitration. Mutual-consent entry (clauses A, B) means no grievance is forced into the fast track. *(clauses A, B, D)*

## ⚠️ Watch-outs
- **Time-limited trial** — MOA takes effect on ratification and **terminates March 30, 2029** unless HEABC and NBA mutually agree to extend. The faster process is not permanent. *(final clause)*
- **No precedential value** — every RDR decision is "without prejudice," limited to the dispute at issue, and cannot be cited in any later proceeding. Speed comes at the cost of building usable case law for members. *(clause H)*
- **Stripped-down due process** — submissions capped at 10 minutes, **no witnesses**, case law limited to one submission, documentation kept minimal, and the Registrar can modify the rules. Fine for simple files; weak if a "non-complex" grievance turns out to need evidence. *(clause F)*

*(Note: PDF page numbers not stated in the changes file header; this is new Appendix FF.1, signed in Joint Caucus 20 April 2026.)*

# MOA – HEABC Membership for Unionized LTC/AL Operators — Gains & Losses
Source: `changes/moa-heabc-membership-ltc-al-operators.md` · Baseline: none (new instrument; MOH/HEABC/NBA)

**Tally:** ✅ 2 gains · ❌ 0 losses · ➖ 0 neutral · ⚠️ 3 watch-outs

## ✅ Gains
- **Extends NBA contract coverage to more nurses** — reverses the 2009 policy that let publicly funded LTC/AL operators avoid HEABC membership and bargain cheaper deals. Operators meeting criteria transition into HEABC, and HEABC/NBA will negotiate a template Transition Agreement to move Facilities-bargaining-unit employees onto the **NBA Collective Agreement**. This is coverage expansion, not just admin. *(clauses 4, 6)*
- **Anti-subcontracting condition** — continued wage-levelling funding is made contingent on **no subcontracting** of work currently done by unionized staff, protecting existing union jobs. *(clause 3)*

## ⚠️ Watch-outs
- **Phased over 2 years** — transition runs **Oct 1, 2026 – Sept 30, 2028**: Phase One (to Sept 30, 2027) targets 50% of qualifying unionized operators, Phase Two the remainder. "Target," not guaranteed, and requires regulatory amendments to the *Health Care Employers Regulation*. *(clauses 7, 8)*
- **Eligibility gated by funding threshold** — only operators meeting "HEABC membership criteria" (Health Organization receiving majority provincial funding, services ≥ $250,000/yr) transition. Smaller or privately funded operators are excluded. *(clause 1)*
- **Wage-levelling can be cut for non-qualifying operators** — MOH commits to wage levelling only "until at least March 31, 2027" for qualifying operators; for others currently receiving it but not meeting criteria, MOH may end it on 90 days' notice. Government already announced it will stop levelling for fully privately funded operators — those nurses may lose parity. *(WHEREAS clauses + clause 2)*

Confirm the executed text fixes a real date; an undefined deadline weakens accountability. *(clause 6, PDF p.161)*

# General Housekeeping Proposal — Gains & Losses
Source: `changes/moa-general-housekeeping-proposal.md` · Baseline: multiple (per item)

> The MOA's own preamble calls these "housekeeping … not intended to substantively alter" rights. That is mostly true, but NOT entirely: it deletes six MOAs/appendices outright, and at least two of those carried live (if niche) entitlements. Effective on ratification of the 2025–2029 agreement.

**Tally:** ✅ 0 gains · ❌ 2 losses · ➖ 11 neutral · ⚠️ 3 watch-outs

## ❌ Losses
- **Appendix Q deleted — path to REGULAR status for home-support client-specific nurses removed.** App Q let a nurse working 15–37.5 hrs/wk in client-specific assignments for >4 months convert to regular status (with displacement/replacement protections). Pure deletion, no relocation. The parties had flagged it dormant/under-review since 1998, but it is still in the in-force agreement, so for any nurse relying on it this is a real lost conversion route. Companion deletions strip the matching casual category (11.04(A)(9)), its 487.5-hr probation (11.04(J)(2)), and the split-shift carve-out (26.02(1)). *(App Q + Art 11.04, 26.02; PDF p.155–161 / 3–4 of 28)*
- **Appendix PP deleted — Primary & Community Care transition protections gone.** Removes the commitment that nurses transitioning to primary/community care get an individual learning-needs assessment with any education gap filled *before* being required to do the work, plus the change-management/Labour Adjustment Plan and clinical-resource-nurse funding. Framed as implementation/transition language, but the "education before required work" safeguard was a concrete protection. *(App PP; PDF p.463–525 / 12–13 of 28)*

## ➖ Neutral / Admin
- **Art 37.04 Domestic & Sexual Violence Leave relocated VERBATIM to new Art 41** (Art 41 retitled Public Office → Domestic and Sexual Violence; the old Public Office text moves up to Art 36.02). Entitlement unchanged: 5 paid + 5 unpaid days + up to 15 weeks additional unpaid, benefit continuity, casual carve-out, legislation-prevails clause all preserved. *(Art 37.04 → 41; PDF p.251–297 / 6–7 of 28)*
- **Appendix P Incentive Payment (Pre/Post-Retirees) relocated VERBATIM to Art 49.0X.** Annual payment = what Employer would have contributed to MPP/PSPP, payable after Dec 31, to RRSP or direct — word-for-word the same. *(App P → Art 49.0X; PDF p.543–599 / 14–15 of 28)*
- **Appendix N (Community-Based flexible-work / Munroe arbitration principle) deleted — no loss.** The Northern Interior Health Unit / Munroe (1996) interpretation principle for OT and shift premiums on flexible schedules was **already stated in the body of Art 25.07(H)**; the MOA just deletes the now-redundant Appendix N and the "(See Appendix N)" cross-ref. Substance preserved. *(App N / Art 25.07(H); PDF p.527–541 / 14 of 28)*
- **Art 46.02 Indigenous ceremonial/cultural/spiritual leave restated "five (5) days" → "thirty-seven point five (37.5) hours."** FTE-neutral for standard 7.5-hr/day staff (5 × 7.5 = 37.5). NOT a cut — see watch-out for compressed-week caveat. *(Art 46.02(a); PDF p.431–435 / 10–11 of 28)*
- **Art 38 "Maternity" → "Pregnancy" gender-neutral reword throughout** (incl. heading, 38.01–38.06, plus 11.04(A)(8) and 13.03(b) cross-refs). MOA expressly states no change to benefits/entitlements; all weeks (17 pregnancy / 61 + 62 parental / 87% SEB allowance) unchanged. *(Art 38, 11.04, 13.03; PDF p.846–982 / 24–27 of 28)*
- **Cross-reference renumbering corrected (no substance change):** 11.03(B) Art 46→60; 21.01 & 22.01 Art 64→62; 60.04 "46.01/46.02/46.03"→"60.01/60.02/60.03"; App A 14.2 Art 46→60; 25.05(A) "25.05(E)"→"25.06(E)". Pointers only — none alter an entitlement. *(One real but non-entitlement change rides along here: **61(B) adds "and 3" to the Labour Relations Code s.50 exclusion** — i.e. it broadens which statutory subsections are carved out of the agreement. Operative, but it changes no nurse's entitlement.)* *(various; PDF p.305–445 / 8–11 of 28)*
- **Art 53.03 RPN differential — statutory reference modernized.** "Nurses (Registered) Act / Nurses (Registered Psychiatric) Act" → "RN and RPN under the BC Health Professions and Occupations Act." Still $50/month; eligibility (dual RN+RPN registration) unchanged. *(Art 53.03; PDF p.379–383 / 9–10 of 28)*
- **College/statute name updates** throughout App RR and JJ.3: "Health Professions Act"→"Health Professions and Occupations Act"; "BCCNP"→"BCCNM." Naming only. *(App RR, JJ.3; PDF p.601–645 / 16 of 28)*
- **Art 32 / App D OH&S language cleanup** (large but cosmetic): "Joint Occupational Health and Safety Committee" spelled out once then abbreviated "JOHSC"; "healthful"→"healthy", "behavioral"→"behavioural", "co-operation"→"cooperation", "&"→"and", PHC/CSA abbreviations defined. No duties, funding ($1,290,000/annum unchanged), or obligations altered. *(Art 32, App D; PDF p.649–840 / 17–23 of 28)*
- **Appendix HH (Job Descriptions) deleted — SPENT.** Its only operative deadline (reduce to ≤60 job descriptions per Health Authority by March 31, 2014) is more than a decade past; a fully obsolete one-time consolidation commitment. *(App HH; PDF p.63–75 / 1–2 of 28)*
- **Appendix JJ.4 (Rural & Remote Nursing) deleted — SPENT.** A one-time joint review tied to a prior PCA's ratification timeline with a one-time $2,000,000 allocation; the review window has long closed. *(App JJ.4; PDF p.77–109 / 2 of 28)*

## ⚠️ Watch-outs
- **Appendix JJ.2 (Specialty Education) deleted — funding floor disappears with no replacement shown here.** Old MOA guaranteed funding for ≥850 specialty-education FTEs (FY2016–17 + balance of that agreement). Largely time-spent, BUT the deletion removes any standing specialty-ed funding commitment from the agreement. If specialty-education funding is not secured elsewhere in the 2025–2029 settlement, this is a quiet loss — confirm against the funding/education MOAs. *(App JJ.2; PDF p.459–461 / 11 of 28)*
- **Art 46.02 — compressed-workweek Indigenous staff should confirm equivalence.** "37.5 hours" exactly equals 5 days only at 7.5 hr/day. Staff on longer compressed shifts should verify they are not effectively limited to fewer than 5 calendar days of ceremonial/cultural/spiritual leave. *(Art 46.02(a); PDF p.435 / 11 of 28)*
- **Appendix Q deletion (see Losses) — niche but real.** Any current home-support client-specific casual relying on the 15–37.5 hr regular-status conversion loses that route; affected members should confirm whether they already hold regular status or have another path. *(App Q; PDF p.155–209 / 4–5 of 28)*
